newsitem.title: USA: Perrigo gets tentative FDA okay on analgesic.
newsitem.headline: Perrigo gets tentative FDA okay on analgesic.

text.p: Perrigo Co said Tuesday that it received tentative approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to manufacture naproxen sodium tablets.
With the approval, Perrigo said it will be in a position to begin shipping this analgesic product to customers on January 12, 1997.

Perrigo said the tentative approval is subject to the expiration of market exclusivity for Aleve, a nationally advertised brand of naproxen sodium, on January 11, 1997. Aleve is made by Roche Holding AG.
Thomas Ross, vice president of investor relations for Perrigo, said Aleve, an over-the-counter product, was given three-year exclusivity in 1994.
With the expiration of that exclusivity, Perrigo can now market a private label, or store brand, version of naproxen sodium, Ross said.
Perrigo said the FDA concluded that naproxen sodium was the bioequivalent to Aleve.

"We are very pleased to receive the FDA's approval of naproxen sodium," Mike Jandernoa, chairman, said in a statement. "Although this product is only one of many over-the-counter pharmaceuticals that Perrigo markets as a store brand, it is significant because it is a new (abbreviated new drug application) and the third received by our company in the last 12 months."
